groups.text: It is currently 20 degrees and raining in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Twenty-one Filipino seafarers returned to Manila on August 15 following separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, Malaysia, and the northern Black Sea. According to the Department of Migrant Workers, three crew members from the M/V Abu Al Abyad were repatriated after their vessel faced projectile attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Seven sailors from the M/V En Ocean returned after their ship broke down and was abandoned in Malaysia, while 11 crew members from the M/V Europe I were removed before a planned voyage through high-risk areas in the Black Sea. Upon arrival, the workers received financial assistance and medical checks. In other news, the European Space Agency has released video from its Mars Express orbiting the Schiaparelli Crater. The crater measures 460 kilometers across but appears relatively shallow, possibly filled over billions of years by lava, water, or wind-blown sediment.

Ukraine is struggling to pass rule-of-law reforms in parliament, failing to fulfill any of the ten points in the Kachka-Kos plan. There are also concerns that the country may be backsliding on certain aspects of judicial reform. During a visit to Kyiv on August 18, Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot told Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha that these EU requirements are not simply meant to please Brussels. Prevot argued that an independent judiciary and bodies capable of fighting corruption are primarily for Ukraine's own benefit. He stated these changes are designed to protect citizens, reinforce trust, and make the country more resilient. While he commended the democratic energy of young Ukrainians holding institutions to account, the tension remains high. The day after these remarks, Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau conducted a raid on an office, highlighting the friction between political goals and actual enforcement.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have formed a joint defense pact in Mecca, establishing that an attack on one member is an attack on all three. Signed on August 7, the agreement binds Islamabad more tightly to Middle Eastern security as Saudi Arabia seeks new partners amid uncertainty over the US security umbrella. While Pakistan aims to turn its long-term military training of Saudi forces into broader strategic influence, former Indian Ambassador Ajay Bisaria suggests the pact will not significantly change the confrontation between India and Pakistan. In other news, Sophie Adenot became the first French woman to perform a spacewalk on Tuesday. She spent nearly six and a half hours outside the International Space Station with American astronaut Anil Menon attempting to replace a communication antenna. Meanwhile, Microsoft warns that Windows 11 version 24H2 Home and Pro editions will stop receiving security updates on October 13.

Apple is attempting to settle its long-running dispute with the European Commission over the Digital Markets Act by revising the commercial terms for apps distributed within the European Union. This latest update follows a previous attempt in June 2025 that was widely criticized as overly complex. Under the new model, Apple will apply a five percent Core Technology Commission to apps distributed via the web or alternative stores, though developers must now track and report these transactions monthly. For applications that direct users to external sites to finalize purchases, Apple will collect a fifteen percent commission. Those enrolled in specific programs, such as Small Business or Video Partner, will pay ten percent. Meanwhile, commissions for in-app purchases are set at twenty percent. These changes signal a potential truce between the tech giant and Brussels after years of regulatory conflict.

Ship management has shifted toward crisis management as geopolitical instability intensifies existing pressures like crew shortages and decarbonization requirements. Irene Rosberg of the Copenhagen Business School notes that when trade routes become unsafe, managers must turn diversions into operational plans. Rerouting vessels around the Cape of Good Hope to avoid Red Sea disruptions adds thousands of nautical miles to Asia-Europe voyages. This increases fuel consumption and complicates emissions targets, while GPS spoofing in high-tension areas further impairs navigation. In a different sphere of discovery, researchers in Japan have identified two new species of blind crustaceans from the genus Bogidiella. Found in the subterranean waters of the Ryukyu Islands, these shrimp-like animals lack eyes and pigmentation to survive in total darkness. One species was found in a submarine cave on Minamidaito island, while the other inhabits fresh water within a cave on Ishigaki island.

German prosecutors are pursuing the extradition of a second suspect in the 2022 explosions that disabled the Nord Stream pipelines. Croatian police recently detained Vladimir Z., a Ukrainian national and trained scuba diver, in Pula under a European arrest warrant. Authorities strongly suspect he jointly caused the blasts that rendered both Nord Stream 1 and 2 inoperable. This follows the arrest of another Ukrainian national in Italy last year. The original sabotage occurred just months after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, aiming to permanently disrupt gas deliveries and cut off revenue Moscow used to finance its military operations. While Germany believes the attack was ordered by unspecified Ukrainian state entities, Kyiv has denied any involvement. These pipelines were designed to deliver Russian gas to Germany and other European nations, but they have remained out of service since the September 2022 attacks.

Oracle has released 943 new security patches as part of its August 2026 Critical Security Patch Update. The company's advisory identifies more than 1,000 unique vulnerabilities across two dozen products, including over 460 bugs that can be exploited remotely without authentication. More than 150 of these defects are critical-severity bugs, with nearly 90 scoring a 9.8 or higher on the CVSS scale. Fusion Middleware and Hyperion received the most fixes this month, at 262 patches each. In separate news from the maritime sector, Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines has become the first cruise line to sign the Merchant Navy Welfare Board’s Seafarer Pledge. Inspired by the Armed Forces Covenant, the pledge commits the company to practical actions that support career progression and ease transitions between sea and shore-based roles for its crew. This follows the company's recent introduction of a dedicated Crew Welfare Officer role.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will bring rain with temperatures between 19 and 24 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your work calendar has Optikrunde at ten in the morning and a group meeting with Gregor at three in the afternoon. Your personal calendar has an all-day event for summer holidays in Berlin.
Mail worth checking: Amazon sent a notification that your package was delivered and picked up by your neighbor, Jacob.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
